target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown, so the existing shared workspace bootstrap cap (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, exported from `src/agents/workspace.ts`) is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read — and reusing it avoids introducing a second size authority. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Exact head:** `cd3cf83e4caeada7cba332ea0b89b4481df2e9d5` (rebased onto latest `upstream/main`).

### CLI transcript proof (exact head, redacted)

Actual `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` output at this exact HEAD (**09908298**). The `--dev` flag isolates state under `~/.openclaw-dev/`; stale plugin config warnings are redacted for brevity.

**Test 1 — Normal identity file (normal.md):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/normal-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...config warnings redacted...]
{
  "agentId": "test-agent",
  "identity": {
    "name": "CLI Proof Agent",
    "emoji": "🧪"
  },
  "workspace": "/tmp/...",
  "identityFile": "/tmp/.../normal-identity.md"
}
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 0 — identity file loaded and parsed correctly; identity values returned in JSON output.

**Test 2 — Oversized identity file (2,097,153 bytes = cap + 1):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/oversized-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...state migration output redacted...]
Identity file /tmp/oversized-identity.md exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 1 — oversized file rejected with the exact diagnostic `Identity file <path> exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes`. No identity configuration was written.

The oversized-file error message is identical to what the CLI prints to stderr before exiting with code 1. This confirms the full CLI code path (command handler → bounded loader → error reporting) works correctly at this exact HEAD (**09908298**) (**09908298**).

### Focused regression tests (exact head)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (10 tests) 386ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Includes `returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap`, which writes `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1` bytes and asserts the `null` fallback.

### Code overview

- `loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` now reads via `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES })`, reusing the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit; read failures and oversized files flow through the existing `null` fallback.
- `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` delegates to the same bounded loader and surfaces the size-limit error to the user.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` and `src/commands/agents.identity.test.ts` cover a normal load and an oversized file at `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1`.
